text:
incident-bot: ALERT 1769992468 - routing-policy errors spike in us-west-2 (automatic pager triggered)

sara: seeing 500s and model-mismatch errors for a handful of customers. metric: routing_policy.error_rate up ~18% over 5m. logs show lots of "variant_not_found" followed by cross-region fallback attempts.

mike: acked. paging eng-oncall, i'm on mobile. tagging @raj for routing policy history.

eng-oncall-bot: @mike you are the current on-call (rot: eng-sre). Use /oncall handoff if needed.

raj: on it. any request ids or short example traces?

sara: pasted a sample trace (redacted):
```
trace_id=abc123 route: customerA -> model: rdx-2b-q4 -> variant: rdx-2b-q4-v2 (not found) -> fallback -> region: us-east-1 -> model: rdx-2b-8bit
error: variant_not_found; fallback_count=3; latency spike 600ms
```

katy: I think this started right after the config-schema rollout that removed `allow_fallbacks` as an explicit field. New parser treats missing field as `true` (legacy code assumed false). customers that relied on no-fallback are now being routed across regions.

mike: oh no. that would explain cross-region failovers. is the old field named exactly `allow_fallbacks` in the routing policy?

katy: yes, it used to be:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  prefer_local: true
  allow_fallbacks: false   # deprecated, used by some tenant overrides
```
new schema expects `fallback_policy: "none"|"regional"|"best_effort"` and defaults to `best_effort`. our schema-migration script didn't map missing `allow_fallbacks=false` -> `fallback_policy: none` for tenant overrides.

raj: status: customers impacted? any high-priority tenants?

sara: initial list: 3 enterprise tenants with strict locality SLAs, ~2% of global qps during peak. errors mainly 500s and response mismatches. Support already has a few escalations.

mike: mitigation plan options: 1) hotfix config loader to treat missing `allow_fallbacks` as `false` for tenant overrides (fast), 2) global emergency policy override to enforce `fallback_policy: none` for affected tenant ids (safer, immediate), 3) rollback schema change (bigger). thoughts?

opsbot: Running quick impact query: tenants affected: tenant-22, tenant-81, tenant-314. total qps impact ~120 rps at peak. estimated customer-visible errors ~1500 in last 10m.

raj: do 2) + 1). push emergency override and then a minimal patch to config loader to map old field. we should avoid full rollback if possible.

sara: started emergency policy override: `rbac-admin apply-override --tenants tenant-22,tenant-81,tenant-314 --set routing_policy.fallback_policy=none`

sara: override applied, waiting for propagation.

(2m later)

katy: metrics: routing_policy.error_rate dropping. cross-region requests reduced. latency returning to baseline for affected tenants.

mike: nice. create a temporary dashboard note and tag support for customer comms.

raj: creating a short postmortem draft: root cause = schema change removed deprecated `allow_fallbacks` field and new default mapping resulted in unintended `best_effort` fallback behavior; missing migration mapping for tenant-level overrides.

sara: noted. will open a Jira for cleanup + tests to block this class of default drift.

katy: patch landed in config-loader repo: 1) map missing `allow_fallbacks=false` -> `fallback_policy: none` for tenant overrides, 2) add schema validation that rejects ambiguous/deprecated mixes, 3) unit tests. CI green. requesting canary deploy to staging.

mike: can we also add an emergency toggle in Console to force `fallback_policy` at org level? this would have allowed manual mitigation without CLI.

raj: good idea; add as a follow-up. i'll file design ticket.

(handoff)

mike: i'm handing off to @raj for overnight monitoring. i've paged support leads and notified customer success for affected tenants. any pending tasks for on-call?

raj: on overnight watch. will monitor the override propagation and error rates every 15m. if we see re-occurrence, escalate to SRE lead.

sara: support update sent: "We've applied a configuration override to ensure your requests stay within the requested region and are no longer subject to fallbacks. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a root cause summary."

katy: follow-ups for postmortem: timeline of events, config schema diff, migration script logs, list of affected tenant overrides, and recommended Console guardrails.

mike: final note: incident classified Sev2 (customer-impacting routing misconfig). mitigated by emergency override + loader patch. owners: katy (fix), raj (monitor/handoff), sara (customer comms).

eng-oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: mike -> raj at 2026-03-15T21:18:40Z.

incident-bot: incident 1769992468 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Close when metrics stable for 6h. :white_check_mark:

raj: acknowledging. I'll update slack thread with final closure time and short follow-up note in ~6h. :thumbsup:
